info.title: /dev/accounting API
info.summary: GoBD-compliant German double-entry accounting as an API.
info.description:
API-first, GoBD-compliant German accounting platform by /dev/null GmbH.

## Machine authentication

A deployment selects one exclusive trust boundary. Public machine deployments
use `AUTH_MODE=machine`: send `Authorization: DPoP <access-token>`, a signed
`DPoP` proof and the target public `ten_` handle in `X-Accounting-Tenant`.
The issuer is `https://auth.d0.eu`; the OAuth resource and sole token audience
are `https://api.d0.eu/accounting`. This resource is distinct from the canonical
HTTP base `https://api.d0.eu/accounting/v1` and silent alias
`https://api.accounting.d0.eu/v1`. Sign each proof for the actual public host,
method and path; query and fragment do not participate in the proof URI match.
Access tokens use PS256 and DPoP proofs use ES256. Client authentication at the
issuer uses `private_key_jwt`, with a separate key from the DPoP proof key.

A `401 use_dpop_nonce` response supplies `DPoP-Nonce`. Retry with that nonce
and a newly signed proof with a fresh `jti`; retain the same Idempotency-Key
when retrying a mutation. Never reuse a proof, including across API instances.
Each operation requires the intersection of token scopes, current identity
grants and local membership permissions. Revocation and permission checks
precede idempotent response replay.

Each operation publishes its required machine scope in
`x-d0-machine-scopes`. A contract test compares this value with the actual
authorization table; it is independent of the legacy assertion deployment.

Authentication failures are `401 invalid_token` or `401 invalid_dpop_proof`;
missing permissions are `403 insufficient_scope`. These responses carry a
DPoP `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. An expired authorization checkpoint fails
closed with `503 security_projection_stale`; unavailable authorization state
or verification keys produce `503 security_projection_unavailable`.
Legacy gateway assertion deployments explicitly select `AUTH_MODE=assertion`
and retain the bearerAuth contract. Machine mode never falls back to Bearer
credentials or client-supplied internal assertion headers. The security
alternatives below describe deployment modes, not interchangeable credentials.

## Isolated customer test environment

The separate test deployment uses the sole OAuth resource and audience
`https://api.test.d0.eu/accounting`, the canonical API base
`https://api.test.d0.eu/accounting/v1`, and a different database, runtime
login, authorization snapshots, and HMAC keys. Production tokens and clients
cannot cross into test or vice versa. The test API exposes only the synthetic
account, open-period, unposted-draft, and trial-balance operations listed in
`docs/accounting-test-environment.md`; no posting, archive, export, webhook,
provider, payment, or mail side effect is available there.

## Accounting Console human BFF

The separate human management surface is
`https://api.d0.eu/accounting/console/v1`. It accepts only PS256 Bearer access
tokens for client `developers.accounting.d0.eu`, sole audience
`https://api.d0.eu/accounting`, and the current signed human membership
roster. `GET /status` and owner-only `POST /activation` establish a tenant;
`GET /limits` reports shared organization and client quota state. With
`X-Accounting-Tenant: ten_...`, the selected tenant, membership, and webhook
endpoint management routes use the same bodies and schemas as the paths
below. Redacted delivery diagnostics and audited replay are specified in
`docs/accounting-console.md`. Human console requests never accept machine
DPoP credentials or client-supplied organization authority.

On the test deployment, the BFF uses client
`developers.accounting.test.d0.eu`, sole audience
`https://api.test.d0.eu/accounting`, and
`https://api.test.d0.eu/accounting/console/v1`. The test Console has
activation, status, limits, tenant and membership management. Its closed
`/explorer` subpath maps only the synthetic operations in
`docs/accounting-test-environment.md` to the same request/response schemas
below, under the current human roster and Accounting-local permissions.

## Money

Amounts are exchanged as an object of an exact integer string in **minor
units** and an ISO-4217 currency — `{"amount": "150000", "currency": "EUR"}`
is 1500,00 €. Never parse an amount into a binary floating-point type.

## Idempotency

Every mutating request MUST carry an `Idempotency-Key`. Replaying a key with
the same complete request replays the original response verbatim; reusing it
with a different body media type (`Content-Type`), body, query, or conditional
`If-Match` validator is rejected with `422 idempotency-key-reused`. A request
whose key is still in flight gets `409 request-in-progress` and may be retried.

## Errors

Failures are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). The stable, machine-readable
discriminator is `type`; `title` and `detail` are prose and may change.

## Events

Posting a Buchung emits a durable `journal_entry.posted` event. Terminal
document archive, preservation, validation, and ZUGFeRD generation results
emit `devacc.async-event.v1` envelopes. Subscribe with `eventTypes: []` to
receive these and future topics; explicit topic filters currently select only
`journal_entry.posted`. Their matching,
active endpoint recipients and each recipient's routing URL are snapshotted
when the event is committed. Delivery attempts are signed with HMAC-SHA256
and may be repeated (see the `webhooks` section). Consumers MUST dedupe on
`event_id`; only journal events carry `resource.seq` for ordering.

get.description: Returns immutable global reference rules. An empty list means no qualified rules are published; ordinary consumer-owned taxKey remains valid.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Rule ID returned as nextCursor by the previous page.

200.description: Bounded page of rules, ordered by ID.

post.summary: Calculate tax from an explicitly selected published rule
post.description: Calculates an exact amount using the selected rule and its effective dates. It makes no posting or legal classification decision.

requestBody.description: Explicit rule, booking date and net amount; no classification is inferred.

200.description: Exact calculation and immutable rule evidence.

get.summary: Read mapped Bilanz and GuV for one fiscal year
get.description:
Requires accounting.read. An explicit immutable mapping classifies every
account with posted activity in the selected fiscal-year/currency/asOf view. Unknown or foreign year
and mapping IDs return 404; missing account classification returns
422 incomplete-account-mapping, including accounts with zero net activity.
Amounts use only booking dates inside the year and the inclusive asOf
posting cutoff. Earlier years are excluded: opening balances must be
ordinary evidence-backed entries or carryforward in this year.
Automated fiscal-year closing entries are excluded so they cannot erase
GuV movements or count the result twice in equity. Other posted entries,
including opening and Storno, contribute normally. A stale asOf yields a
historical report, not an assertion that finalization has occurred.

Mappings and labels are supplied by the integrator, never inferred from
account numbers or tax keys. Asset and expense amounts are debit minus
credit; liability, equity and income use the opposite sign. result is
income minus expense; balanceDifference is assets minus liabilities,
equity and result. Each currency is separate. This is an accounting
report under the chosen mapping, not statutory filing validation.

Data sorts by classification, reportCode and currency; account drilldowns
sort by the mapping's frozen accountNo then accountId. Follow accountId
to its statement with the response dates and asOf. That statement also
contains closing entries; use closingEntryIds to reconcile their exclusion.
Empty views return empty arrays. More than 10000 account/currency rows
returns 413 report-too-large; any signed-int64 amount overflow fails the
whole response with 422 balance-overflow.

parameters.name: fiscalYearId
parameters.description: Fiscal year whose inclusive dates delimit posted activity.

parameters.name: mappingRevisionId
parameters.description: Immutable consumer-owned account classification.

200.description: Bilanz and GuV sections with account drilldowns and currency totals.

get.description: Returns fiscal years in start-date order for the calling tenant.

post.description: Creates an open fiscal year with inclusive dates; tenant years cannot overlap.

requestBody.description: Consumer-selected fiscal-year dates and label.

get.description: Returns one year of the calling tenant.

post.description:
Requires exact coverage by contained, festgeschrieben periods and no
unposted drafts in the year. Finalization is irreversible. A fresh-key
replay returns the original finalization time. P&L closing is optional;
carryforward incorporates any remaining income or expense balance.

Derives every currency's income and expense balance from posted entries
inside this year using an immutable caller-selected mapping. Posts inverse
lines against an explicit equity result account with one archived Beleg,
then seals the closing period in the same transaction. All other periods
must already be sealed. If all P&L balances are zero, the period is sealed
and entries is empty. A repeat with identical inputs returns the prior result.

requestBody.description: Closing period, mapping, result equity account and archived Beleg.

200.description: Posted closing entries and sealed period.

post.summary: Post an opening balance into the next fiscal year
post.description:
Source year must be finalized; target starts on the following day. For
one currency, derives source-year posted balances under the selected
immutable mapping. Asset, liability and equity balances carry to the same
accounts; remaining income and expense net goes to the explicit equity
result account. The target year must have no earlier posted entries in
that currency. One archived Beleg is attached to the ordinary journal
post. A fresh-key retry with identical inputs returns the existing entry;
a different transfer for either source or target year conflicts.

requestBody.description: Target, immutable mapping, result account, currency and Beleg.

200.description: Posted opening entry or its existing representation.

get.summary: Read a complete Summen- und Saldenliste at one posting cutoff
get.description:
Requires accounting.read. Returns posted opening, debit, credit and closing
amounts per account and currency, plus currency totals.
Uses the same asOf and inclusive date filters as account balances. Drafts
never contribute; Storno contributes its ordinary opposite lines. accountNo comes from the latest participating posted line by seq/lineNo,
including opening history. Renumbering without a new posting cannot alter
a report, and all numbers of one account aggregate together. Rows sort by accountNo,
accountId and currency; totals sort by currency. Unused accounts/currencies
are omitted, including with a currency filter; empty views use empty arrays.
Positive balances are debit, negative credit. This is cumulative history,
not a fiscal-year report; use financial-statements for year-scoped reporting.
A maximum of 10000 rows including totals is returned atomically; exceeding
the bound is 413 report-too-large. Every amount must fit signed int64 minor
units, including gross currency totals; otherwise 422 balance-overflow.
No partial or rounded report is returned.

200.description: Complete account rows and per-currency control totals.

get.description: Returns published mapping revisions in ascending version order for this tenant.

post.description: Freezes explicit consumer classifications and account labels for reproducible reports. Every reportCode must have one classification and name.

requestBody.description: Complete consumer-owned account classification and report labels.

get.description: Returns the complete frozen mapping if it belongs to this tenant.

200.description: Immutable mapping revision with its complete account items.

post.summary: Retire an account for future ordinary postings
post.description: Retirement is irreversible and serializes with posting. Historical reads and exact Storno remain available; fresh-key retirement retries preserve the original timestamp.

get.summary: Download a complete tenant accounting snapshot
get.description:
Requires explicit exports.read permission and accounting.exports.read
machine scope. Returns a devacc.tenant-export.v1 ZIP containing versioned
JSON datasets, a manifest with SHA-256 checksums, and available archived
document originals verified against their immutable evidence. Includes
discarded drafts, pending declarations, and public archive disposition
receipts. A confirmed original deletion retains its document metadata and
receipt but excludes its bytes. A deletion in progress returns retryable
409 before ZIP bytes are sent.
All metadata comes from one tenant-scoped database snapshot. Original
versions are pinned by that snapshot and verified before any ZIP bytes
are sent. Stored journal hashes and sequence links are evidence; the
public projection does not contain the private canonical hashing payload.

The synchronous export is limited to 100000 records, 32 MiB of metadata,
512 MiB of original bytes and two minutes of preparation (the authorization
lease may expire sooner). Exceeding a size limit returns 413 export-too-large;
no successful truncated export is returned. Unavailable originals return
503 and integrity mismatches return 502. Range and conditional headers do
not select a partial result. Verify Content-Length and Content-Digest after
download; interruption or authorization expiry may truncate transport.

200.description: The complete verified ZIP, downloaded as an attachment.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment with a generated tenant export filename.

Content-Digest.description: RFC 9530 SHA-256 digest of the complete ZIP bytes.

Content-Length.description: Exact byte length of the ZIP.

get.description: Requires explicit access.manage in the bound tenant. This grants administration across that tenant's authoritative partner. Ordered by public identifier; after is an exclusive public identifier boundary, not a snapshot.

post.description: Requires explicit access.manage in the bound tenant. This grants administration across that tenant's authoritative partner. Creates a tenant and inherits the administrator membership's explicit permissions for the same identity.

requestBody.description: Explicit access provisioning fields.

get.description: Requires explicit access.manage in the bound tenant. This grants administration across that tenant's authoritative partner. Ordered by public identifier; after is an exclusive public identifier boundary, not a snapshot.

post.summary: Grant an external identity tenant access
post.description: Requires explicit access.manage in the bound tenant. This grants administration across that tenant's authoritative partner. The subject belongs to the configured trusted issuer; permissions must be supplied explicitly.

requestBody.description: Explicit access provisioning fields.

put.description: Requires explicit access.manage in the bound tenant. This grants administration across that tenant's authoritative partner. Uses expectedRevision to prevent lost updates; inactive memberships cannot access the tenant.

requestBody.description: Explicit access provisioning fields.

get.description: Accounts of the calling tenant, ordered by Kontonummer.

post.description:
Adds a Konto to the tenant's chart of accounts. `accountNo` is unique per
tenant; creating a duplicate is `409 account-already-exists`.

requestBody.description: The Konto to add.

get.description: Returns the account if it belongs to the calling tenant, else 404.

get.summary: Read a posted Kontoblatt at a fixed booking state
get.description:
Requires accounting.read. Returns individual posted lines for this account
in ascending Buchungsnummer (seq), then lineNo order. Drafts are excluded.
Multiple lines in the same Buchung remain distinct. Date bounds are inclusive;
currency filters never convert amounts. accountNo is the frozen number as
booked, not current chart metadata. Follow entryId to the journal entry or
GET /documents?journalEntryId={entryId} for its immutable Beleg links;
document reads require documents.read separately.

Without asOf, captures the latest committed tenant-wide posted entry. The
response's asOf can be reused across statements and balances. Later posts,
including backdated entries, newly posted old drafts and later Storno, are
excluded. This freezes posted evidence, not mutable chart data or a complete
tenant export. The literal empty fixes an empty ledger even after later posts.

Pass nextCursor as after and keep date/currency filters unchanged. The cursor
carries the original snapshot, so asOf may be omitted on subsequent pages.
An explicit conflicting asOf or a malformed, foreign or nonmatching cursor
is 400 invalid-cursor. Unknown, foreign or draft asOf entries are
400 invalid-snapshot. Any committed posted entry can define a historical
cutoff, even if it belongs to another account or currency in this tenant.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque nextCursor from this account and the same date/currency filters.

200.description: A page of immutable posted account movements.

get.summary: Read exact account totals and balances by currency
get.description:
Requires accounting.read. Only posted lines contribute, including Storno
through their normal opposite sides. Uses the same asOf cutoff and inclusive
date/currency filters as the account statement. Omitted asOf captures the
latest committed tenant-wide posted entry; reuse the returned value to keep
subsequent reads fixed. Unknown, foreign or draft snapshots are
400 invalid-snapshot. The literal empty always returns an empty ledger view.

openingBalance is debit minus credit strictly before bookingDateFrom, or
zero without a lower bound. debitTotal and creditTotal cover the selected
date range. closingBalance is openingBalance plus debitTotal minus
creditTotal. Positive balances mean debit; negative balances mean credit,
independently of account type. This is cumulative posted history, not a
fiscal-year opening or carry-forward operation. Currencies are never mixed
or converted and results are ordered by currency code.

With no currency filter, returns currencies with posted activity through
bookingDateTo (including opening history); otherwise an unused currency
returns one zero row. A wholly unused account has data: [] without a currency
filter. All returned totals must fit signed int64 minor units; any overflow,
including gross debit/credit totals with a representable net, fails the whole
response with 422 balance-overflow. No rounded or partial totals are returned.

200.description: Exact totals per currency at the returned posting snapshot.

get.description: Periods of the calling tenant, ordered by start date.

post.description:
Periods of one tenant may not overlap; an overlapping range is
`409 period-overlap`. A new period starts `open`.

requestBody.description: The period to open.

get.description: Returns the period if it belongs to the calling tenant, else 404.

post.description:
Permanently seals the period. The database records the authoritative
transition time and actor; neither value is caller-controlled. A fresh-key
retry after an uncertain response is domain-idempotent and returns the
existing terminal Period with its original `festgeschriebenAt`.

Draft Buchungen may remain in the period, but they can no longer be posted.
Festschreibung is irreversible; corrections remain new Storno entries.

200.description: The sealed period, or its unchanged terminal representation.

get.description:
Entries of the calling tenant in ascending immutable entry-ID order,
independent of booking date and posting sequence. Select `draft` or
`posted` explicitly. Date bounds are inclusive and combine with periodId.
Optional documentId restricts results to entries directly linked to that
Beleg, including Storno entries with inherited links. Requires accounting.read;
it returns journal data, not document metadata. Unknown or foreign documentId
is 404 document-not-found. The optional externalReference filter uses an
exact, case-sensitive match (no wildcards, trimming or Unicode normalization).
References are not unique: an original and its Storno share the reference.
Keep filters unchanged when passing nextCursor as after. The cursor must
identify an entry visible to this tenant, even if it no longer matches
the filters; malformed, unknown or foreign cursors are 400 invalid-cursor.
Pagination is not a snapshot: concurrent commits and mutable drafts or
status transitions can change membership between requests. Entries that
become eligible before the cursor are not revisited; restart traversal
to rediscover them. Unchanged data is traversed without skips or duplicates.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The nextCursor from the previous page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Select drafts or posted entries.

parameters.name: periodId
parameters.description: Restrict to this tenant's accounting period.

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: Only entries directly linked to this tenant's Beleg.

parameters.name: bookingDateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive earliest booking date.

parameters.name: bookingDateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive latest booking date; must not precede bookingDateFrom.

parameters.name: externalReference
parameters.description: Exact business reference; combines with all other filters. U+0000 is forbidden.

200.description: A page of journal entries with their lines.

post.description:
Creates an unposted (draft) Buchung and its lines. The draft is validated
immediately — at least two lines, every amount positive, Soll and Haben
equal, one currency throughout — but it takes no `seq` and enters no hash
chain until it is posted. A draft in a period that is already
festgeschrieben is rejected at post time, not here.

requestBody.description: The Buchung to draft, with all of its lines.

get.summary: Fetch one Buchung with its lines
get.description:
Returns the Buchung and its lines in line order. A draft carries no `seq`,
`entryHash` or `postedAt`; a posted one carries all three.

put.description:
Replaces all draft accounting fields and lines. Omitted optional metadata
is cleared. Identity, creation evidence and linked Buchungsbelege remain.
Posted entries reject changes with `409 entry-not-draft`. Requires the
latest item ETag; stale versions return `412 precondition-failed`.

requestBody.description: The complete replacement accounting content and lines of the draft.

delete.description:
Discards an unposted draft from item and list reads. Linked archived
Buchungsbelege remain preserved. Posted entries reject discard with
`409 entry-not-draft`. Requires the latest item ETag.

post.description:
Finalizes a draft: it is assigned the tenant's next `seq` (the legal
Buchungsnummer), linked into the append-only hash chain, and becomes
immutable. A `journal_entry.posted` event is emitted in the same
transaction — the entry and its event commit together or not at all.

Posting is terminal. Corrections are new reversal entries (Storno), never
edits. Posting an entry that is not a draft is `409 entry-not-draft`;
posting into a period that is festgeschrieben is `409 period-sealed`.
At least one archived Buchungsbeleg must already be linked to the draft;
otherwise posting is rejected with `422 beleg-required`.
Optional If-Match binds posting to the reviewed draft revision under the
posting lock. A stale version returns 412 without posting; omission
preserves unconditional posting for existing clients.

Creates and immediately posts a new immutable Storno. The server copies
the original currency, lines, frozen Kontonummer snapshots and immutable
Beleg evidence, swaps Soll and Haben, and sets `reversalOf` to the target.
A `journal_entry.posted` event is emitted in the same transaction.

The caller selects an open destination period and a booking date within
that period because the original period may already be festgeschrieben.
Only posted entries can be reversed. A second direct reversal is rejected
with `409 entry-already-reversed`; reverse the Storno itself to undo it.
Retry an uncertain response with the original `Idempotency-Key` for an
exact replay; a fresh key represents a new write intent.

requestBody.description: The destination period and Buchungsdatum for the Storno.

201.description: The newly created and posted Storno.

post.summary: Link an archived Beleg to a draft Buchung
post.description:
Links an archived Buchungsbeleg to a draft. The link is append-only and is
included in the entry's audit hash when the Buchung is posted. Pending
documents and entries that are already posted are rejected.

204.description: The document is linked. Repeating the link is a no-op.

get.description:
Requires documents.read. Returns public metadata in ascending immutable
document-ID order, independent of Belegdatum. Omitted filters include all
documents; provided filters combine with AND. Date bounds are inclusive.
journalEntryId selects direct links to a Buchung (including inherited
Storno links), without exposing journal data. sourceDocumentId selects
direct generated outputs, never transitive descendants. Unknown or foreign
relationship IDs are 404; an existing resource with no matches gives an
empty page. Read each output's sources to inspect source roles.

Pass nextCursor as after with unchanged filters. The cursor must name a
document in this tenant, even if it no longer matches the filters;
malformed, unknown and foreign cursors are 400 invalid-cursor. Pagination
is not a snapshot: concurrent commits and pending-to-archived transitions
may change membership. Documents that become eligible before the cursor
are not revisited; restart traversal to discover them. Unchanged data is
traversed without skips or duplicates.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The nextCursor from the previous page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict to pending or archived documents.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Restrict to uploaded originals or generated derivatives.

parameters.name: documentDateFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive earliest Belegdatum.

parameters.name: documentDateTo
parameters.description: Inclusive latest Belegdatum; must not precede documentDateFrom.

parameters.name: journalEntryId
parameters.description: Only documents directly linked to this tenant's Buchung.

parameters.name: sourceDocumentId
parameters.description: Only direct derivatives of this tenant's source document.

200.description: A page of public document metadata.

post.description:
Creates a pending Buchungsbeleg and returns a short-lived, create-only PUT
request for a direct upload. The checksum, exact byte length, media type,
and COMPLIANCE Object Lock retention are all covered by the signature.

`classification`, storage identity, retention policy, and retention horizon
are server-owned. This public workflow always creates `buchungsbeleg`.

requestBody.description: Immutable metadata known before the upload starts.

201.description: The pending Beleg and its first direct-upload request.

get.summary: Read the direct sources of a generated Beleg
get.description:
Requires documents.read. Returns the immutable direct source references,
ordered by role. Uploaded originals return an empty data array. Currently
the only derivation kind is zugferd-pdf, with exactly one invoice source
and one visual source; this bounded set needs no pagination. Sources are
visible as soon as a derived document is declared, including while it is
pending. Each documentId can be resolved through GET /documents/{documentId}.
Storage keys, object versions and internal identifiers stay private.

200.description: The complete, bounded set of direct source references.

get.description:
Returns public lifecycle and declaration metadata. Storage keys, immutable
object version ids, actor ids, and internal database ids are never exposed.

Requires documents.read and an archived Beleg visible to the tenant.
Returns the complete original bytes from the recorded immutable object
version after verifying length and SHA-256. No storage coordinates or
download credentials are disclosed. Partial and conditional requests are
not supported; Range and conditional headers do not select another result.
Pending documents and a deletion in progress return 409. A confirmed
original deletion returns 410; document metadata and the disposition
receipt remain available. Missing or unavailable archive objects return
503; inconsistent archive bytes or metadata return 502 before any file bytes
are sent. Clients should verify Content-Digest and Content-Length as well.

200.description: The verified original bytes, downloaded as an attachment.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment with the validated original filename.

Content-Digest.description: RFC 9530 SHA-256 digest of the complete original bytes.

Content-Length.description: Exact byte length of the original.

post.summary: Create a fresh upload request for a pending Beleg
post.description:
Re-signs the pending document's original immutable declaration. Use a fresh
`Idempotency-Key` after an earlier signed request expires. An archived Beleg
can never receive another upload URL.

post.summary: Verify and archive an uploaded Beleg
post.description:
Verifies the exact immutable object version, checksum, length, media type,
and COMPLIANCE retention before atomically sealing the Beleg. Retrying the
same completed upload is safe.

post.summary: Request stronger preservation of an archived Beleg
post.description:
Requires documents.write. Records the requesting actor, reason and requested
protection without changing the original Beleg evidence. Requests may extend
COMPLIANCE retention, set a legal hold ON, or both. Shortening, hold release
and deletion are not supported. An extension must exceed the original storage
deadline and every previously accepted extension for this Beleg.

A 202 response confirms durable acceptance only. Poll the returned resource;
applied means the worker has verified the requested protection on the original
immutable object version. Storage outages leave the request pending for retry.
Replaying the same Idempotency-Key returns the original acceptance response;
use GET for current state. The retentionUntil on the original Document remains
its initial, immutable policy evidence.

requestBody.description: A reasoned retention extension, legal-hold ON request, or both.

202.description: The durable preservation request, awaiting storage confirmation.

Location.description: Relative URL for polling the request within this API base.

get.summary: Fetch a preservation decision and its confirmed application state
get.description:
Requires documents.read. The request and actor attribution are immutable.
appliedAt and observed protection are present only after exact-version storage
verification. A completed observation is historical evidence, not a live
storage availability probe. Storage coordinates and credentials are not exposed.

200.description: The tenant-visible request and its application state.

post.summary: Queue validation of an archived XML e-invoice
post.description:
Creates one durable validation request for the exact immutable object
version sealed into the archived Beleg. The service submits those bytes
to the standalone compliance platform under a deployment-pinned validation
policy, then copies the verified exact result into its own immutable GoBD
archive before publishing completion. Processing is asynchronous; poll the
resource named by `Location` until its status is `completed` or `failed`.
A completed validation with `result.valid: false` is a successful validation
outcome, not a processing failure.

Only archived `application/xml` Belege up to 20 MiB (20,971,520 bytes)
are accepted. The source bytes and storage identity are never exposed by
this operation.

202.description: The validation was durably queued, or an exact idempotent replay.

Location.description: Relative URI of the durable validation status resource.

get.description:
Returns the durable validation state if it belongs to the calling tenant,
else 404. Terminal validation results include the exact validator and
ruleset identities frozen by the standalone compliance platform. A
processing failure exposes only a stable public code; internal diagnostics
never cross this boundary.

200.description: The validation request and its current state.

post.summary: Queue creation of an immutable ZUGFeRD PDF
post.description:
Combines the exact CII XML from a completed, valid e-invoice validation
with one immutable archived PDF visual source. Processing is durable and
asynchronous; poll the resource named by `Location` until it is terminal.

The server selects and freezes the ZUGFeRD standard, EN 16931 profile, and
generation recipe. The original XML and visual Belege remain independently
archived; the output is a new immutable derived Beleg with explicit lineage.
UBL-to-CII conversion and visual rendering are deliberately not implicit.

requestBody.description: Selects the already archived PDF visual source.

202.description:
The generation was durably queued. An exact Idempotency-Key replay
returns its originally stored response; the same semantic request under
a new key returns the already existing durable resource in its current
state, which may already be terminal.

Location.description: Relative URI of the durable ZUGFeRD PDF status resource.

200.description: The generation and its current state.

get.description:
Requires explicit webhook endpoint management permission in the calling
tenant. Returns every endpoint of that tenant, including inactive endpoints,
ordered by creation time. Inactive metadata remains visible so an endpoint
can be audited or reactivated without losing its identity or delivery history.

200.description:
A page of webhook endpoint metadata. Collection responses do not carry
per-item HTTP validators; fetch an item before mutating it to obtain its
current `ETag`.

post.description:
Requires explicit webhook endpoint management permission in the calling
tenant. Registers an active HTTPS destination. The caller supplies the
signing secret once; it is write-only and is never included in this or any
later response. A tenant may retain at most 256 endpoints in total, including
inactive endpoints, and at most 64 of them may be active. Deactivation does
not free retained-endpoint capacity.

requestBody.description: Destination, subscription, and caller-generated signing secret.

201.description: The created endpoint metadata. The signing secret is never returned.

get.description:
Requires explicit webhook endpoint management permission in the calling
tenant. Returns safe metadata if the endpoint belongs to that tenant, else
404. The signing secret is never readable through the API.

put.description:
Requires explicit webhook endpoint management permission in the calling
tenant. Fully replaces the destination URL, event subscription, and active
state; the existing signing secret is unchanged. All three metadata fields
are required.

The active state and event subscription select recipients only for events
committed after this replacement commits. Each previously selected recipient
keeps the routing URL snapshotted with its event, even if this replacement
changes the URL. Setting `active` to false also permanently suppresses every
older-snapshot recipient for this endpoint that a worker has not already
loaded. Reactivating the endpoint later does not revive those suppressed
recipients; it only makes the endpoint eligible for new event snapshots. An
attempt loaded before deactivation commits may still complete with its pinned
URL after this operation returns.

requestBody.description: Complete replacement metadata for the endpoint.

delete.description:
Requires explicit webhook endpoint management permission in the calling
tenant. Soft-deactivates the endpoint. No endpoint or delivery-attempt row is
deleted: its stable identity, lifecycle attribution, and delivery audit
history are preserved.

After deactivation commits, the endpoint is excluded from new event snapshots
and every older-snapshot recipient for it that a worker has not already loaded
is permanently suppressed. Reactivating the same endpoint identity later does
not revive those suppressed recipients. Deleting an already inactive endpoint
is a no-op. An attempt loaded before deactivation commits may still complete
with its pinned URL after this operation returns.

204.description: The endpoint is inactive and its audit history is preserved.

put.summary: Rotate a webhook endpoint signing secret
put.description:
Requires explicit webhook endpoint management permission in the calling
tenant. Replaces only the signing secret; metadata and active state are
unchanged. Configure the receiver to accept both secrets before rotating.
Once this operation returns 204, every newly loaded attempt uses the current
secret version, including a retry for an event snapshotted before rotation.
A request already loaded or in flight may still arrive with a signature made
by the old secret. Keep the overlap until those attempts have drained. The
old and new secrets are both write-only and are never returned.

requestBody.description: The caller-generated replacement signing secret.

204.description: Future delivery attempts use the replacement secret.

post.summary: An asynchronous document or e-invoice operation reached a terminal result
post.description:
Delivered to active endpoints with `eventTypes: []`. The event-time
recipient and route snapshot, HMAC signatures, retry and deduplication
rules are identical to `journalEntryPosted`. Fetch the named public
resource for current details; the envelope contains no document bytes,
validation report, internal ID, or sequence number.

parameters.name: D0-Signature
parameters.description: The published v1 HMAC signature; see `journalEntryPosted`.

parameters.name: D0-Signature-V2
parameters.description: The preferred authenticated-header HMAC; see `journalEntryPosted`.

parameters.name: D0-Webhook-Id
parameters.description: The authenticated `event_id`, stable across redelivery.

default.description: Not acknowledged; the delivery may be retried.

post.description:
When the event is committed, its recipients are snapshotted from the tenant's
active endpoints subscribed to `journal_entry.posted`; each selected recipient
also pins that endpoint's routing URL. Later URL or subscription changes do
not retarget that event. A later deactivation permanently suppresses a selected
recipient that a worker has not already loaded, even if the endpoint is then
reactivated. An attempt already loaded when deactivation commits may complete.

Delivery attempts may be repeated: the same `event_id` can arrive more than
once, and events can arrive out of order. Every newly loaded attempt uses the
endpoint's current signing-secret version. Dedupe on `event_id` and order by
`resource.seq`. Existing integrations can continue verifying `D0-Signature`.
New and upgraded integrations should verify `D0-Signature-V2`, which also
authenticates `D0-Webhook-Id`, before trusting the body. Return any 2xx status only after the
event is durably recorded; any 2xx marks this recipient successful. Connection
failures and non-2xx responses may be retried under the current delivery policy.
Attempt limits, timing, backoff, and transient/permanent classifications are not
part of this contract and may evolve. Receivers SHOULD allow at least five minutes
of signature timestamp tolerance; this covers the bounded fan-out, normal network
delay, and ordinary clock skew.

parameters.name: D0-Signature
parameters.description:
Backwards-compatible signature with the published v1 wire format:
`t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is lowercase hexadecimal
HMAC-SHA256(endpoint secret, `"<unix-seconds>." + raw request body`).
The header is retained byte-for-byte for existing consumers. It authenticates
the timestamp and exact body, but not the separate `D0-Webhook-Id` header.
Compare in constant time and reject a timestamp outside your tolerance window.
A tolerance of at least five minutes is recommended.

parameters.name: D0-Signature-V2
parameters.description:
Preferred signature: `t=<unix-seconds>,v2=<hex>`, where `v2` is the
lowercase hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of the following versioned binary message:

`"d0.webhook.v2" || 0x00 || int64be(t) || uint64be(len(id)) || id ||`
`uint64be(len(body)) || body`

Here `id` is the exact ASCII value of `D0-Webhook-Id`, `body` is the
exact raw request body, and both lengths count bytes. Compare the MAC in
constant time and reject a timestamp outside your tolerance window. The
timestamp, webhook ID, and body are all covered by the MAC, so none can be
substituted independently. A tolerance of at least five minutes is recommended.

parameters.name: D0-Webhook-Id
parameters.description:
The envelope's `event_id`, repeated as an authenticated header so a
receiver can dedupe a redelivery without parsing the body. It is included
in the `v2` signature message and is byte-identical to the body field.

requestBody.description: The event envelope. Verify the signature before parsing it.

204.description: Acknowledged. This recipient is marked successful.

2XX.description:
Acknowledged with another 2xx status. Every 2xx status marks this
recipient successful.

default.description:
Not acknowledged. The delivery may be retried under the current policy;
retry count and schedule are not contractual.

machineToken.description:
Machine-only AUTH_MODE=machine. DPoP-bound PS256 access token issued by
https://auth.d0.eu for the sole audience https://api.d0.eu/accounting.
Use Authorization: DPoP <token>; Bearer and internal assertions are denied.

machineProof.name: DPoP
machineProof.description:
ES256 dpop+jwt proof binding the token hash, proof key, actual public
method/URI, current issued-at time, fresh unique jti and server nonce.
On 401 use_dpop_nonce, retry with DPoP-Nonce and a fresh proof jti.

must permit that tenant and operation.

Opaque event identifier — the deduplication handle for webhook delivery. Like
every identifier this API publishes it is minted independently of the row it
names, so it encodes neither a primary key nor the order events were created in.

A terminal asynchronous result. `succeeded` means processing completed;
a validation can still report `valid: false` when read through its resource.

tenant_id.description: Opaque public tenant UUID, never its internal database ID.

Stable, machine-readable problem identifier. This is the field to
branch on; `title` and `detail` are prose and may be reworded.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

WebhookEndpointSecretReplace.description: Write-only replacement signing material for one endpoint.

WebhookEndpointSecret.description:
Exactly 32 bytes encoded as canonical, unpadded base64url (43 characters).
For every create or rotation, the caller MUST generate a unique, independent,
unpredictable 32-byte value with a cryptographically secure random-number
generator and MUST NOT reuse it for another endpoint or secret version. The
caller retains this HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. It is accepted only on create
or rotation and is never returned by the API. The final-character restriction
rejects non-canonical encodings with non-zero unused bits.

WebhookEndpointId.description:
Opaque webhook endpoint identifier. It encodes neither the tenant nor the
endpoint's internal database identity.

WebhookEndpoint.description: Safe webhook endpoint metadata. Signing-secret material is never present.

active.description:
Whether this endpoint is eligible for newly committed event snapshots.
Deactivation also permanently suppresses its older-snapshot recipients
that a worker has not already loaded; later reactivation does not revive
those recipients.

updatedAt.description:
Last metadata, active-state, or secret change. A secret rotation changes
this timestamp but never exposes either secret.

WebhookEndpointEventTypes.description:
Unique event types delivered to this endpoint, with at most 16 entries.
An empty array subscribes the endpoint to all current and future webhook
event types; list explicit values to opt in only to those event types. The
subscription is evaluated when each event's recipients are snapshotted;
changing it does not add or remove recipients from an existing snapshot.

WebhookEventType.description: A domain event type currently available for endpoint subscriptions.

WebhookEndpointURL.description:
Absolute HTTPS delivery URL of at most 2,048 UTF-8 bytes. Userinfo and
fragments are forbidden, and an IP-literal host must be globally routable;
loopback, private, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, multicast, documentation,
unspecified, and other special-use addresses are rejected. On create and
replacement, the service canonicalizes an accepted URL before storing and
returning it: the scheme and ASCII host are lowercased, the default HTTPS
port is removed, and a non-default port is normalized to decimal. The caller
does not need to perform that canonicalization first.

DNS names are resolved only when delivery is attempted: the complete answer
set is validated and the selected public address pinned before every connection
to prevent rebinding. Redirects are not followed. URL syntax and IP-literal
restrictions are rechecked whenever metadata is replaced and again at delivery
time. Query strings are retained in immutable routing history for audit and
retries; they must not contain credentials or capability tokens. Authenticate
delivery with the signing secret instead.

WebhookEndpointReplace.description:
Complete replacement of mutable endpoint metadata. The signing secret is
deliberately not metadata and remains unchanged.

PreconditionRequired.description:
This mutation requires the latest item `ETag` in `If-Match`; no
resource state or audit evidence was changed.

Unprocessable.description:
The request is well-formed but cannot be carried out — an unbalanced
Buchung, or an `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different request (including
a different `Content-Type` or `If-Match` validator).

PreconditionFailed.description:
The supplied `If-Match` validator is well-formed but stale. No resource
state or audit evidence was changed. Fetch the item and retry the
intended change with its new `ETag` and a fresh `Idempotency-Key`.

Conflict.description:
The request conflicts with current state — a duplicate, a sealed period, an
entry that is no longer a draft, or an in-flight request with this
`Idempotency-Key`.

Retry-After.description:
Present only on `request-in-progress`, where the conflict is transient:
a duplicate of this request is still running and retrying after the
given number of seconds will succeed. Absent on the other conflicts,
which retrying cannot resolve.

NotFound.description: No such resource in the calling tenant.

Forbidden.description:
The caller is authenticated for the tenant but lacks the explicit permission
required for this operation. No data is read or written.

Unauthorized.description: No valid tenant assertion. No data is read or written.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or violates the contract.

WebhookEndpointETag.description:
Strong opaque validator for this endpoint's routing and signing-secret
version. Send this exact value as `If-Match` on replace, secret rotation,
or deactivation. Operational KEK rewrapping does not change it.

ActingUserRecorded.description:
Present with exactly v1 on successfully committed partner-attributed
machine writes and their idempotent replays. Absent on unattributed writes.
An attributed consumer must qualify this acknowledgment before presenting
success. Missing acknowledgment leaves an unknown attribution outcome.

JournalEntryETag.description: Strong opaque validator bound to the entry identity and revision.

WebhookEndpointIfMatch.name: If-Match
WebhookEndpointIfMatch.description:
The exact strong `ETag` returned by the latest item response. Weak tags,
wildcard matching, and validator lists are not accepted because every
mutation must name one observed endpoint version. A missing precondition is
`428 precondition-required`; a well-formed but stale validator is
`412 precondition-failed`. After a 412, fetch the item and retry the intended
change with its new `ETag` and a fresh `Idempotency-Key`.

ActingUserSubject.name: X-Accounting-Acting-User-Subject
ActingUserSubject.description:
Stable opaque person reference in the issuer namespace, asserted by the
authenticated partner. Send exactly one value together with
X-Accounting-Acting-User-Issuer; 1–200 ASCII bytes without whitespace or
commas. Use technical references, not names or email addresses. A different
attributed human or asserting machine under the same Idempotency-Key is
a different request (422). Neither header is an Accounting membership ID.

ActingUserIssuer.name: X-Accounting-Acting-User-Issuer
ActingUserIssuer.description:
Optional partner-attested human attribution, machine authentication only.
Send exactly one value together with X-Accounting-Acting-User-Subject.
Absolute HTTPS issuer URI without credentials, query or fragment; ASCII
without whitespace or commas. The authenticated partner asserts this
identity; Accounting does not independently verify a human login token.
This metadata grants no tenant access or permissions and never replaces
the authenticated machine membership. Retained as immutable same-transaction
evidence with the write and included in the idempotency fingerprint.
Successful attributed writes and their replays return
X-Accounting-Acting-User-Recorded: v1. Deploy this API before enabling
attributed writes; a missing acknowledgment leaves the outcome unqualified.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-generated key that makes this mutation replay-safe. Send exactly
one field value. Use a fresh value (a UUID or equivalent) per logical
operation and reuse it verbatim when retrying that operation.

One layer of surrounding double quotes is stripped before the key is
compared, so the RFC 8941 structured-field form (`"k"`) and the bare form
(`k`) name the same key.

WebhookEndpointId.name: webhookEndpointId
WebhookEndpointId.description: Identifier of the tenant-managed webhook endpoint.

WebhookEndpointCursor.name: after
WebhookEndpointCursor.description:

JournalEntryPostIfMatch.name: If-Match
JournalEntryPostIfMatch.description:
Optional strong item ETag of the reviewed draft. Checked under the same
lock as posting. A stale revision returns 412; omission preserves the
existing unconditional posting behavior. Weak tags, wildcards, duplicate
values and lists return 400. A failed request rolls back its key and can
reuse it after reviewing the current draft. Use a new Idempotency-Key
for a new intent after a previously successful request.

JournalEntryIfMatch.name: If-Match
JournalEntryIfMatch.description:
Exactly one strong item ETag observed from create, GET or replacement.
Weak tags, wildcards and lists are rejected with 400. Missing tags return
428; stale tags return 412. Fetch again and retry with a fresh
Idempotency-Key after a stale version.
